title: Sicilian Defense: Najdorf Variation
line: A quiet pawn move keeps White's pieces out, then a center pawn kicks the knight away.

steps.text: The usual Sicilian start: White pushes the king's pawn, Black answers from the side, and White pushes a second center pawn.
Black trades its side pawn for that center pawn, and both sides bring a knight out.
Push the pawn on a7 one square. It keeps White's knight and bishop off b5.

also.g7g6: That is the Dragon, another main line. This lesson goes on with the Najdorf.
also.b8c6: That is the Classical Variation, another main line. This lesson goes on with the Najdorf.
also.e7e6: That is the Scheveningen, another main line. This lesson goes on with the Najdorf.

steps.text: Push the pawn on e7 two squares. It kicks the knight out of the center.
Bring the bishop to e6. It watches d5, the hole in front of your pawn that White's pieces want.

also.f8e7: That is also played. This lesson brings this bishop out first.

steps.text: Bring the other bishop out, so you can castle.
Castle. Your king is safe and a rook joins the game.
steps.after: White castles on the other side. Each side will now push pawns at the other king.

steps.text: Bring the other knight to d7. It guards your pawn on e5 and keeps the way clear for the pawn on b7.
steps.after: White's pawns start their run at your king.

steps.text: Push the pawn on b7 two squares, toward White's king. Next it can push on and hit the knight on c3, which guards e4.
steps.after: This is the Najdorf race: each side throws pawns at the other king, and the faster attack counts.

summary: The Najdorf keeps White's pieces off the side square, kicks the knight from the center, then races pawns at the king.
